speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me how long these skin lesions have been present and whether they are itchy or painful?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-year-old female. The patient's mother reports noticing multiple painless, nonpruritic papules on the child's abdomen. The child attends daycare where another child was reported to have similar lesions recently. Patient's brother had chickenpox one month ago. Immunizations are up-to-date.

speaker: Doctor
text: Are the papules umbilicated, meaning do they have a small central dimple? I would like to check if any of the lesions are located on the child's face or extremities as well.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Skin-colored, nontender, pearly papules with central umbilication on the abdomen and extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: The clinical presentation of umbilicated, pearly papules in a child with recent exposure is highly suggestive of Molluscum contagiosum. DIAGNOSIS READY: Molluscum contagiosum
